sites.evidence_type: published tolerance of a different insertion (transposon, FP fusion)
sites.functional_impact_measured: The construct was used to report surface-displayed DCC in neurons; the clip describes it as designed for this purpose but does not report a quantitative functional assay result beyond surface-reporting utility. NOT MEASURED for netrin-1 binding or axon guidance function.
sites.rationale: L3 explicitly states pHluorin was 'inserted in position 1090' of rat Dcc. Python confirms that in the human DCC canonical sequence, residue 1090 = V and residue 1091 = T, and position 1090 falls within the extracellular span (26–1099), 10 residues from the TM boundary (1100), satisfying the ≥3-residue clearance rule. The rat Dcc ortholog is a close ortholog; the topology is conserved. The insert_after_residue=1090 interpretation (tag between V1090 and T1091) is consistent with 'inserted in position 1090' meaning at the codon for residue 1090. A rat Dcc-pHluorin construct was engineered by inserting a pH-sensitive GFP at position 1090 of Dcc (rat ortholog), creating a surface-reporting construct used in neuronal studies. The construct is full-length and membrane-anchored, designed to report surface-displayed DCC.

sources.claim: Expression plasmids for LacZ, Pard3a, Siah2, Siah2ΔRING, and H2B-mCherry were subcloned as previously described 6 , 7 pCIG2 Dcc-pHluorin (Dcc-pH), with a pH-sensitive form of green fluorescent protein (GFP) 50 inserted in position 1090, was obtained from Franck Polleux at Columbia University.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: Flow cytometry on transiently transfected HEK293T cells confirmed cell-surface expression of the FLAG-tagged full-length DCC construct.
sites.rationale: The ledger (L1/L2) reports a full-length, membrane-anchored human DCC construct with an N-terminal FLAG tag whose DCC portion begins at H26 (the mature N-terminus after signal-peptide cleavage at residue 25). Python confirms residue 25 = A and residue 26 = H. The tag is placed after residue 25 (insert_after_residue=25), which is the only extracellular N-terminal junction available once the signal peptide is cleaved. Surface expression was validated by flow cytometry (L2). Full-length human DCC (H26–I1442) expressed in HEK293T cells with an N-terminal FLAG tag inserted after the signal-peptide cleavage site (residue 25), creating a membrane-anchored construct. The construct description 'H26-I1442' explicitly anchors the DCC mature sequence starting at H26, placing the FLAG between residue 25 and 26.

sources.claim: N-terminal flag-tagged (MGGTAARLGAVILFVVIVGLHGVRGKDYKDDDDKLE), full-length and deletion constructs for human DCC are as follows: Flag-DCC full-length (H26-I1442); Flag-DCC Ig1-4 (H26-S425-BamH1-L1098-I1442); Flag-DCC FN1-6 (S426-I1442), Flag-DCC FN4-6 (E722-I1442).

literature_notes: L1 and L2 both ground the same N-terminal FLAG site; L2 is the surface-expression confirmation of L1's construct, so they are treated as one site with L1 as the primary clip. L4 (Δcyto-3xHA) places a 3xHA tag at the C-terminus of a truncated rat Dcc construct ending at residue 1125, which is intracellular (TM ends at 1120); this is recorded in other_positions. L5 (DCC-HaloTag) places HaloTag at the C-terminus of full-length human DCC (residue 1447), which is also intracellular; recorded in other_positions. Neither L4 nor L5 qualifies as a surface tag site. The pHluorin site (L3) is from rat Dcc but is treated as a close ortholog with conserved topology; position_evidence is 'validated' because the paper names residue 1090 explicitly, but confidence is medium because it is a rat construct and the functional impact on DCC signaling was not measured.

literature_other_positions.note: 3xHA tag placed at the C-terminus of a rat Dcc truncation construct ending at residue 1125 (3 residues into the intracellular domain, TM ends at 1120); this is an intracellular tag, not a surface tag site.
HaloTag fused to the C-terminus of full-length human DCC at residue 1447, which is intracellular; not a surface tag site.
